title: Iniön kirkon peruskorjaus - RU, LVIA, S, ML, SPR
description: Paraisten seurakuntayhtymä pyytää tarjousta Iniön kirkon peruskorjauksesta. Iniön kirkko sijaitsee Iniön alueseurakunnan toiminta-alueella. Kirkko on yksi yhteensä kymmenestä kirkosta ja kappelista Paraisten seurakuntayhtymän alueella. Seurakuntayhtymän muodostavat alueen kaksi seurakuntaa: Väståbolands svenska församling ja Länsi- Turunmaan suomalainen seurakunta. Kirkko on rakennettu vuosina 1797-1800 Gustaf af Sillénin piirustusten mukaan. Kirkko vihittiin kayttöön kesäkuussa 1801 ja se sai nimen juuri syntyneen prinsessa Sofia Wilhelminan mukaan. Kivestä ja tiilestä rakennetun pitkäkirkon itäpuolella sijaitsee satulakattoista runkohuonetta matalampi ja kapeampi sakaristoja länsipuolella kolmikerroksinen kellotorni. Vuosina 1967-68 kirkossa suoritettiin korjaustöita ja sisustus uusittiin osittain. Kirkkoon asennettiin sähkövalot ja keskuslämmitys sekä lattia uusittiin. Kirkon sisäpintoja kunnostettiin vuonna 2000 ennen kirkon 200-vuotisjuhlaa. Tämä tarjouspyyntö sisältää mm. seuraavat korjaustyöt: kosteusvaurioituneen lattiarakenteen uusiminen, peltikaton uusiminen, lämmitysjärjestelmän sekä muu talotekniikan uusiminen. Kirkon sisustukseen tehdään mm. alttari- ja penkkimuutoksia. Hanke toteutetaan jaettuna urakkana. Rakennusteknisten töiden urakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana ja lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana ja työsuojelusta vastaavana osapuolena. Putki-, iv-, sähkö-, sprinkleri- ja maalämpötöiden urakat toteutetaan pääurakkaan alistettuina sivu-urakoina. Tilaaja edellyttää, että urakoitsija on tutustunut rakennuspaikkaan ennen tarjouksen antamista. title: France – Traffic-flow measuring system – RENOUVELLEMENT DES SYSTEMES DE MESURES DU VEHICULE DE MESURE DE LA GEOMETRIE DES VOIES
description: Dans le cadre des projets de maintenance de l’infrastructure patrimoniale du réseau de la RATP, le présent marché a pour objet le renouvellement des systèmes de mesures du véhicule V355 tels que détaillés dans le bordereau de prix, délai de fabrication (Annexe 1). Le véhicule V355 est le moyen de référence utilisé par l’unité Voie pour la recherche, la mesure et le suivi des défauts de géométrie de la voie sur les réseaux Métro et RER. Il permet de contrôler l’état géométrique de l’infrastructure et d’identifier les écarts susceptibles d’impacter la sécurité, la disponibilité et la qualité de roulement. La V355 est équipée d’un système de mesure associant une triangulation laser et une centrale inertielle, permettant d’effectuer une acquisition complète des paramètres géométriques de la voie. Les données collectées lors des campagnes de mesure sont analysées afin de détecter les défauts, de suivre leur évolution dans le temps et de déclencher, si nécessaire, des actions de maintenance ou des dépêches pour les valeurs hors limites. L’exploitation de la V355 repose sur environ 45 campagnes de mesure annuelles, avec une fréquence comprise entre un et quatre passages par ligne et par an, conformément aux pratiques nationales de surveillance des infrastructures ferroviaires. Ces campagnes fournissent une vision exhaustive de l’état géométrique du réseau et constituent un outil d’aide à la décision pour la programmation des opérations de maintenance. Cette consultation donnera lieu à un accord cadre mono-attributaire à bons de commandes comprennant un montant minimum et un montant maximum. Les prestations et fournitures comprises dans le montant minimum sont les suivantes : - Fourniture du système de géométrie o Étude préliminaire d'intégration mécanique et électrique o Fabrication du système complet et des éléments relatifs à l'intégration sur le véhicule o Fourniture des logiciels - Intégration sur le véhicule o Dépose et mise au rebut des éléments constitutifs de l'ancien système o Installation sur le véhicule V355 o Paramétrages - Essais de réceptions o Essais statiques et dynamiques sur réseau RER et métro - Livrables o Cahier de recette o Formation des agents o Documentation technique, plans manuel de maintenance o Fourniture des pièces critiques de rechange Les prestations et fournitures comprises dans le montant maximum sont les suivantes : - Maintenance annuelle - Formation des agents - Système complémentaires o Usure ondulatoire ▪ Fourniture du système ▪ Intégration sur le véhicule ▪ Essais de réceptions ▪ Livrables o Détection de défauts par vidéo ▪ Fourniture du système ▪ Intégration sur le véhicule ▪ Essais de réceptions ▪ Livrables o Barre de courant & voies pneus ▪ Fourniture du système ▪ Intégration sur le véhicule ▪ Essais de réceptions ▪ Livrables o Obstacles et quais ▪ Fourniture du système ▪ Intégration sur le véhicule ▪ Essais de réceptions ▪ Livrables o Entrevoie ▪ Fourniture du système ▪ Intégration sur le véhicule ▪ Essais de réceptions ▪ Livrables - Prestations sur devis La RATP se réserve la possibilité de faire réaliser des prestations similaires par le Titulaire du marché dans les conditions énoncées à l’article R2122-7 du Code de la Commande publique. title: Finland – Fencing, railing and safety equipment installation work – Tikkurilan osaamiskampusalueen Oppilaitoskorttelin tilaturvallisuuskokonaisuuden urakka ja palvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Tikkurilan osaamiskampusalueen Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennuksen tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmäkokonaisuuden urakka ja takuun jälkeisen korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluiden toimitus. Hankinta sisältää tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmien ja niiden hallinta-alustan toimittamisen ja käyttöönoton käyttökuntoon saakka, sekä korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalvelut. Hankinta sisältää seuraavat järjestelmätoimitukset: - Kulunvalvontajärjestelmä - Kameravalvontajärjestelmä - Rikosilmoitinjärjestelmä - Ovipuhelinjärjestelmä - Henkilöturvajärjestelmä - Hätäkuulutusjärjestelmä - Lukitusjärjestelmä - VIRVE-verkko - Järjestelmäkokonaisuuden hallinta-alusta Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus tulee sijoittumaan Tikkurilan osaamiskampuksen alueelle lähelle Tikkurilan asemaa, osoitteeseen Jokiniemenkatu 1, 01370 Vantaa. Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus käsittää opiskelutilat noin 2600 opiskelijalle viidestä eri oppilaitoksesta: Vantaan Ammattiopisto Variasta, Tikkurilan lukiosta, Tikkurilan iltalukiosta, Vantaan aikuisopistosta ja Vantaan Musiikkiopistosta. Lisäksi henkilökuntaa on noin 300. Oppilaitoskorttelissa on kellarikerroksen lisäksi maan päällä kuusi opetustoiminnan kerrosta ja IV-konehuonekerros. Hankesuunnitelman mukainen laajuus on 25 200 brm2 ja tontin pinta-ala on noin 7900 m2. Kohde on toiminnaltaan, sijainniltaan ja turvallisuusympäristöltään poikkeuksellisen vaativa. Kohteen tilaturvallisuudessa on huomioitava useat käyttäjäryhmät, jotka käyttävät kiinteistöä eri tavoin ja eri ajankohtina, sekä laaja määrä julkisia tiloja, joihin on kulku pääsisäänkäynnin kautta. Lisäksi järjestelmätoimituksissa on huomioitava tilojen muuntojoustavuus sekä toimitettavien järjestelmien skaalautuvuus tulevaisuudessa myös muihin kiinteistöihin ja uusille käyttäjäryhmille. Hankittavaan urakkaan kuuluu 24 kuukauden takuuaika ja pidennetyt takuuajat. Työssä noudatetaan urakkatoimituksen osalta YSE 1998 -ehtoja, sekä palveluiden osalta JYSE-palvelut 2025 -ehtoja tarjouspyynnössä ja sopimuksessa esitetyin poikkeuksin. Tilaturvallisuusurakka toteutetaan rakennusurakan alistettuna sivu-urakkana, jossa projektinjohtourakoitsijana (pääurakoitsija ja -toteuttaja) toimii YIT rakennus Oy.

title: Finland – Repair, maintenance and associated services related to roads and other equipment – Vantaan liikennevalojen ja katuverkon liikenteenhallintalaitteiden kunnossapito 2027-2028 (optio 2030)
description: Vantaan kaupunki järjestää yhteishankintana Fintrafficin kanssa tarjouskilpailun Vantaalla sijaitsevien liikennevalo-ohjattujen liittymien liikennevalolaitteiden sekä katualueiden liikenteenhallintalaitteiden kunnossapitopalvelusta hankinta-asiakirjoissa tarkemmin osoitetussa laajuudessa. Kunnossapitopalveluun sisältyviä keskeisimpiä tehtäviä ovat vikapäivystys, vikavalvonta, vianselvitykset ja -korjaukset, liikennevahinkojen korjaukset, laitteiden määräaikaiset tarkastus- ja huoltokierrokset, liikennevalodokumentaation ylläpito sekä muut liikennevaloihin liittyvät asiantuntijatehtävät. Lisäksi Palveluntarjoajan tehtävänä on varaosavaraston ylläpitäminen. Kunnossapitopalvelun puitteissa voidaan toteuttaa liikennevalo- ja liikenteenhallintalaitteiden saneeraustöitä. Palvelun piiriin voidaan sopimuskauden aikana lisätä tai siitä voi poistua liikennevaloliittymiä tai liikenteenhallintalaitteita. Mahdolliset uudet kohteet tulevat sijaitsemaan Vantaan alueella. Palvelun arvioitu sopimuskausi on määräaikainen kaksi (2) vuotta ajalla 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Sopimusaikaa on mahdollista jatkaa yhdellä kahden (2) vuoden pituisella optiolla 1.1.2029 - 31.12.2030. Tilaaja päättää option käyttöönotosta viimeistään kuutta (6) kuukautta ennen varsinaisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Kunnossapitopalvelun tehtävät ja niiden sisältö on määritelty tarkemmin tässä tarjouspyynnössä sekä tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.

description: Hankinnan kohteena on koko Senaatti-konsernin lukitusjärjestelmät ja niihin välittömästi liittyvät tuotteet, ohjelmistot ja palvelut. Tässä hankinnassa tavoitteena on saada vahvat toimittajat valtakunnallisesti tuottamaan ja ylläpitämään Senaatti-konsernin lukitusjärjestelmiä, oviympäristöjä ja fyysiseen pääsynhallintaan liittyviä laitteita sekä järjestelmiä. Itä-Suomen alue, Kouvolan seutu 7. Itä-Suomen alue, Kuopion seutu 8. Pohjois-Suomen alue, Oulun seutu 9. Pohjois-Suomen alue, Rovaniemen seutu. Osa-alueet on nimetty alueella sijaitsevan yhden tai enintään kahden kaupungin mukaan. Kukin osa-alue kuitenkin käsittää nimettyä kaupunkia laajemman kokonaisuuden. Tarkemmat osa-aluekohtaiset kuvaukset on esitetty liitteissä. Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhtä tai useampaa osa-aluetta. YHTEISHANKINTA Senaatti-kiinteistöt toteuttaa hankinnan yhteistyössä muiden samaan konserniin kuuluvien toimijoiden kanssa. Hankintayksikkö järjestää kilpailutuksesta yhden infotilaisuuden torstaina 3.9.2026 klo 10-11. Tilaisuus on vapaaehtoinen. Tarkemmat tiedot Tarjoajainfo-liitteestä. Tilaisuudessa käydään tarjouspyyntö ja tarjouspyyntömateriaali yleisesti läpi. Tilaisuuden tarkoitus on kertoa tarjoajille tarjouspyynnön sisältö ja kannustaa tarjoajia tarjoamaan.

title: Finland – Machine tools – Metrokiskojen ylläpitohiontalaite
description: HKL-liikelaitos (edustajana toimii Pääkaupunkiseudun Kaupunkiliikenne Oy "KLOY") on hankkimassa laahuskivitekniikalla toimivan metrokiskojen hiomakoneen (jäljempänä ”kone”), jolla on tarkoitus torjua alkavia kiskovikoja. Hankinnan tavoitteena on jatkaa kiskojen käyttöikää ja vähentää profilointitarvetta. Koneen hiontatoiminto saa käyttövoimansa koneen diesel-aggregaatista, mutta sitä hinataan tai työnnetään ratakuorma-autolla. Koneen sijoituspaikka on Helsingin metrovarikko, jonne kone myös toimitetaan (DAP Metrovarikko, Helsinki). Kone tulee toimittaa hyväksytysti viimeistään 16 kuukauden kuluessa sopimuksen allekirjoituksesta. Kone puretaan kuljetuksesta toimittajan henkilökunnan opastuksella ja läsnä ollessa sekä saatetaan kiskoille toimintakuntoon. Hankinta sisältää takuuajan huolto- ja varaosat sekä KLOY:n konetta käyttävän henkilökunnan koulutuksen. Kone vastaanotetaan ja hyväksytään tilaajan varikolla henkilökunnan koulutuksen yhteydessä. Tarkempi kuvaus hankinnan kohteesta ja siihen liittyvistä vaatimuksista löytyy seuraavista liitteistä: - 01 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus - 02 Vaatimukset Hankintaan valitaan yksi toimittaja, joka vastaa koko ajoneuvon toimituksesta.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – ikääntyneiden ympärivuorokautinen palveluasuminen
description: Kanta-Hämeen hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia ikääntyneiden ympärivuorokautisen palveluasumisen hankintaan. Kilpailutus sisältää seuraavat tuotteet: 1. Ympärivuorokautinen palveluasuminen, pitkäaikainen 2. Ympärivuorokautinen palveluasuminen, lyhytaikainen Ympärivuorokautinen palveluasuminen on sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014) 21 c §:n mukaista asumispalvelua, jota järjestetään asumisyksiköissä, joissa henkilöstö on paikalla ympäri vuorokauden. Ympärivuorokautisessa palveluasumisessa asiakkaalle tarjotaan aktiivisista asumista ja kuntouttavaa hoivaa esteettömässä, turvallisessa ja kodinomaisessa asuinympäristössä. Palveluasumisen myöntäminen perustuu aina tilaajan toteuttamaan palvelutarpeen arviointiin. Tarjottavan yksikön tulee sijaita Kanta-Hämeen alueella. Toiminnassa olevan yksikön lisäksi on mahdollisuus tarjota myös perustettavaa toimintayksikköä. Mikäli perustettava yksikkö ei ole toiminnassa vielä sopimuskauden alkaessa, voidaan yksikkö lisätä palveluntuottajalistaukseen perustamista seuraavan vuoden alusta alkaen. Perustettavasta yksiköstä tulee ladata perustamissuunnitelma tarjouspyynnön kohdassa "Muut ehdot". Kilpailutuksen perusteella solmittava sopimuskausi on voimassa 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2030. Hankintasopimus sisältää mahdollisuuden jatkaa sopimusta 1 + 1 +1 vuoden optiokaudella. Tilaajan on mahdollista ottaa optiokausi käyttöön Toimittaja-, palvelutuote- tai yksikkökohtaisesti. Optiokautta ei välttämättä oteta käyttöön kaikkien Palveluntuottajien kanssa. Hankinnan kohde ja palvelulle asetetut vähimmäisvaatimukset on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvonlisäveroton kokonaisarvo on enintään 385 miljoonaa euroa. Luku on sitomaton arvio. Tarjouspyynnössä ilmoitettu hankinnan kokonaisarvo on ennakoitu arvo, joka on laskettu koko hankintakokonaisuuden osalta laskennallisen 7 vuoden ajalta, mahdolliset optiot mukaan luettuna. Kilpailutuksessa valitaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät palveluntuottajat. Tarjoushinnan perusteella muodostuu etusijajärjestys. Hankintajärjestelmä ei sisällä määrä- tai vähimmäisostovelvoitetta.

title: Finland – Medical specialist services – Natiiviröntgenkuvien etälausuntapalvelu Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue
description: Hankinnan kohteena on röntgenkuvien (ns. natiivikuvien) etälausuntapalvelu, jossa Toimittajan radiologian erikoislääkärit tuottavat lausuntoja Tilaajan toimittamista kuvantamistutkimuksista OptoMed-portaalin kautta. Palvelu on toimiluvallista arvonlisäverotonta terveydenhuollon palvelua. Palvelu kattaa perusterveydenhuollon natiiviröntgentutkimukset, mukaan lukien esimerkiksi thorax-kuvaukset, tuki- ja liikuntaelinten kuvaukset. Hankinnan kohteeseen eivät kuulu hammasradiologiset eikä rintaradiologiset natiiviröntgentutkimukset. Tilaaja hankkii etälausuntoja tarpeensa mukaisesti, eikä sitoudu vähimmäisostomääriin. Tavoitteena on aloittaa sopimuskausi 15.10.2026. Sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Lausunnot tuotetaan OptoMed-portaalin kautta palvelukuvauksessa tarkemmin kuvatulla tavalla. Arvio tutkimusmäärästä on noin 12 000–15 000 lausuntoa vuodessa. Vertailutietona todetaan, että Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue hankki ostopalveluna vuonna 2024 noin 12 200 ja vuonna 2025 noin 13 700 natiivikuvatutkimuksen lausuntoa. Tiedot on annettu tarjoajien hankinnan laajuuden arvioinnin tueksi, eivätkä ne sido tilaajaa tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Hankinnassa valitaan yksi (1) toimittaja tuottamaan palvelua.

description: 537-2405 - A21 Administration Wheelchair Lift Replacement This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Bowden Institution, Innisfail Alberta Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to replace the institutional grade wheelchair lift in the Administrative Building at Bowden Institution. Background: The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) operates Bowden Institution, an active federal correctional facility. The institution’s Administration Building requires the removal of existing wheelchair lift equipment and the supply, installation, commissioning, and acceptance of a new barrier-free wheelchair lift system. Objectives: The Contractor must deliver a fully operational, code-compliant, institutional-grade wheelchair lift that provides barrier-free access between the upper floor, main floor, and basement, that the contractor as inspected, tested and commissioned, and that CSC has formally accepted for use in an operational correctional environment. Deliverables: The Contractor must keep Site Disruptions (noise, dust, smells, etc.) to a minimum. The Contractor must communicate all anticipated disruptions to the Client Representatives in advance to allow CSC to distribute communications to users. The Contractor must provide Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Manuals, that include the following information as a minimum: a.Manufacturer data b.Maintenance schedules c.Spare parts lists d.Warranty information The Contractor must submit the O&M manuals and as-built drawings to the designated CSC Project Authority for acceptance as a condition of Substantial Completion. Formats: the Contractor must submit O&M manuals in the following format: a)PDF electronic copy to CSC.b) Red Line As-builts: Red Line is to provide the drawings to CSC. title: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä
description: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia kokonaisuudesta, johon sisältyvät: 1. kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille 2. hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu 3. hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä edellä mainitun palvelun tuottamiseen hyvinvointialueen omana toimintana. Hankinnassa turvalaitteilla tarkoitetaan erilaisia kotiin annettavia turvalaitteita, joilla voidaan parantaa kotona asuvan asiakkaan turvallisuutta. Hankittavia turvalaitteita ovat turvapuhelimet ja niiden lisälaitteet, paikantava turvaranneke sekä ratkaisu yhteisöllisen asumisen ovivalvontaan. Hälytysten vastaanottopalvelulla tarkoitetaan palvelua, jossa otetaan vastaan turvalaitteiden kautta tulevat hälytykset, tehdään alustavan arvion avuntarpeesta ja välitetään pyyntö edelleen turva-auttajille. Palvelun tulee toiminnassa vuorokauden ympäri vuoden jokaisena päivä. Hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmällä tarkoitetaan järjestelmää, jolla tilaaja voi ottaa eri turvalaitteiden hälytykset vastaan ja edelleenvälittää ne tehtävänä turva-auttajille. Lapin hyvinvointialueella on tarkoitus ottaa hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu omaksi toiminnaksi alustavan aikataulun mukaan keväällä 2028. Hyvinvointialue hankkii hälytysten vastaanottopalvelua siihen asti, kunnes vastaanottojärjestelmä on otettu käyttöön, minkä jälkeen vastaanottopalvelun hankinta päättyy. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Kilpailutuksessa valitaan yksi toimitta puitesopimustoimittajaksi. Puitejärjestelyn kautta hyvinvointialue hankkii valitulta toimittajalta turvalaitteita ja palveluita sopimuskauden aikana tarpeen mukaan. Hyvinvointialueen tarpeet voivat vaihdella sopimuskauden aikana, eikä tarjouspyynnöllä sitouduta tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Puitesopimuksen sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena kaksi vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Hankintayksikön tarkoitus on tehdä sopimus valitun toimittajan kanssa heti, kun tarjousaika on päättynyt, tarjoukset on vertailtu, hankintapäätös on tehty ja muutoksenhakuaika on päättynyt. Hankintayksikön arvion mukaan ajankohta on lokakuun 2026 aikana. Laitevaihtojen toteutuksen ja muiden käyttöönottoon liittyvien toimien aikataulut sovitaan yhdessä valitun toimittajan kanssa molempien osapuolten tarpeet huomioivalla tavalla. Lisäksi valitulta toimittajalta hankitaan hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä kokonaisuutena, johon sisältyy järjestelmän toimittaminen ja sen jatkuva palvelu. Järjestelmän jatkuvan palvelun sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska kyseessä on yhtenäinen tavaroiden ja palveluiden muodostama kokonaisuus, jonka kaikkien osasten yhteensopivuus on voitava varmistaa. Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaiden turvallisuuden kannalta on tärkeää, että yksi toimittaja vastaa koko kokonaisuuden toimivuudesta. Hankintailmoitus on julkaistu toisen kerran uudelleen, koska kaksi aiempaa hankintamenettelyä on täytynyt keskeyttää hankinta-asiakirjojen muutostarpeiden vuoksi.,

title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

title: Bio-Rad QX600 Droplet Digital PCR System
description: Requirements The laboratory requires a digital droplet PCR (ddPCR) platform capable of absolute nucleic acid quantification with high sensitivity and multiplex capability. The quoted system provides up to six-color multiplex detection, processes up to 96 samples per run, and performs absolute nucleic acid quantification Type of Order: Firm Fixed Price Purchase Order Special Order Requirements: The instrument shall: Perform digital droplet PCR using partitioned droplet technology. Partition each 20 ?L reaction into approximately 20,000 droplets. Support six-color fluorescence detection. Process 96-well plates. Provide absolute nucleic acid quantification without reliance on standard curves. Support applications including: mutation detection copy number variation gene expression viral titer analysis Include software capable of automated thresholding, Poisson analysis, multiplex analysis, and export of results. Include all required computer hardware and system software. Include a compatible thermal cycler capable of operating 96-well deepwell PCR plates. These specifications are consistent with the manufacturer's published technical specifications. The contractor shall deliver the following equipment to the National Institutes of Health (NIH): One (1) Bio-Rad QX600 Droplet Digital PCR System One (1) Bio-Rad PTC Harmony Deepwell Thermal Cycler Training: Training is not included under this purchase. The contractor is not required to provide user training as part of this award.

title: Echodyne EchoShield Radar System
description: The EchoShield is a software-defined, cognitive 4D pulse-Doppler radar operating in the Ku-band (15.4 to 16.6 GHz) that utilizes Echodyne's proprietary Metamaterials Electronically Steerable Antenna (MESA) technology This low size, weight, and power (low-SWaP) system is designed for multi-domain, multi-mission operations, offering a wide field of view (130� azimuth by 90� elevation) and an industry-leading angular tracking accuracy of less than 0.5�. Built to military standards (MIL-STD-810H), the ruggedized, IP67-rated unit can track over 1,000 objects simultaneously and output high-precision data to direct optical sensors and mitigation effectors. Highly versatile and customizable via software waveforms, the EchoShield supports diverse missions --including counter-UAS, ground dismount and vehicle tracking, coastal perimeter security, and on-the-move mobile operations. The 57 RQS requests acquisition of four (4) echodyne echoshield radars, 4 units of EchoShield software uprates and technical support, amd the echodyne rapid deployment kit.

title: Community Residential Facility (CRF) - John Howard Society of Brandon
description: Advanced Contract Award Notice (ACAN) Community Residential Facility (CRF) - John Howard Society of Brandon An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC), as part of the criminal justice system and respecting the rule of law, contributes to public safety by actively encouraging and assisting offenders to become law-abiding citizens, while exercising reasonable, safe, secure and humane control. This includes: • Management of offenders during their transition from the institution to the community, and while on supervision; and • Ensuring the safety and security of members of the public, victims, staff and offenders in the community. While decisions on the conditional release of offenders fall under the responsibility of the Parole Board of Canada, CSC is responsible for supervising offenders under federal jurisdiction on conditional release in the community until the end of their sentences and offenders subject to Long-Term Supervision Orders. Community Residential Facilities (CRFs) provide a bridge between the institution and the community, ensuring that suitable accommodation, support systems and monitoring are in place to assist conditionally released offenders to become law-abiding citizens. The statement of work for CRFs includes, but is not limited to the following: 1.1 Objectives: Provide accommodation, monitoring, general support and assistance to offenders under federal jurisdiction who have been released to the community on conditional release, statutory release, and those subject to Long-Term Supervision Orders. 1.2 Tasks: The CRF must provide twenty-four (24) hour residential services to adult offenders. These services include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Providing beds to offenders referred by CSC and accepted by the CRF; 2. Providing three (3) meals a day. Meals must meet health and nutritional requirements in accordance with Canada’s Food Guide; 3. Developing a Resident Action Plan and monitoring and supporting offender activities against the Community Strategy, Resident Action Plan and Correctional Plan; 4. Assisting offenders in areas including but not limited to: crisis management, personal or family problems, education, literacy, employment, budgeting, life skills; 5. Assisting offenders to secure services appropriate for their needs or for public safety requirements, such as substance abuse services, income support, employment services, medical (including mental health) and dental services; 6. Providing offenders with a supportive group living environment; 7. Providing first aid services to offenders including having a first aid kit available and ensuring at least one staff member on each shift has valid St-John’s Ambulance and CPR certifications; 8. Recording and incorporating pertinent information on individual offenders into the offender case file. Treating all sensitive or protected offender information in accordance with the security requirements of the contract; 9. Providing static and dynamic security services including having staff on-site and awake 24 hours per day, performing offender counts, monitoring offender activities and destinations, and notifying CSC when offenders’ behaviour deteriorates or when offenders abscond from the CRF or are unlawfully at large; 10. Providing Monthly Utilization Reports, Monthly Living Allowance Reports, Incident/occurrence reports as they occur, as requested by CSC; 11. If applicable and where required, the CRF must ensure that the accommodations are suitable and safe for children residing in the CRF with their legal guardian in accordance with CSC policies; 12. In accordance with its needs and at its own discretion, CSC may request that the CRF provide enhanced or specialized services to support the placement of high needs offenders. The services to be provided will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Depending on the CRF/location, the work may also include the following; 1. Delivery of a residential substance-abuse treatment program; 2. Delivery of the Integrated Correctional Program Model; 3. Provision of classroom space for program delivery; 4. Provision of a personal escort, as required, to accompany offenders outside the facility; 5. Provision of personal support worker services for offenders with mental health issues; 6. Supervision of the collection of urine samples and forwarding them for analysis; 7. Provision of In-Reach services; 8. Provision of reporting centre services; and 9. Provision of Indigenous Spiritual Advisory services. 1.3 Expected results: Assisting conditionally released offenders to safely and successfully reintegrate into the community as law abiding citizens. 1.4 Performance standards: The CRF and its officers, servants and subcontractors must comply with all applicable legislation and CSC’s Commissioner’s Directives (CDs), the Standard Operating Practice on Official Languages, and other Standards. The CRF must be in compliance with all applicable territorial, provincial, municipal and local legislation and regulations. The CRF premises and equipment must conform to applicable zoning, health, safety, building and fire codes and regulations. The CRF must have written plans for dealing with fire, medical emergencies (including pandemic situations) and natural disasters, and the CRF staff must be trained accordingly. The CRF must provide a copy of these plans to the Project Authority. The CRF must ensure that staff members, volunteers and students have the qualifications required and receive proper training and orientation prior to assuming responsibility for their duties. The CRF must also provide ongoing training to staff, volunteers and placement students essential for their assigned duties and responsibilities. The CRF must ensure that staff, volunteers and placement students have reached the age of majority in the province of operation. If applicable and where required, the CRF must provide a strategy to accommodate diverse cultures and spiritualties, including, but not limited to, Indigenous culture and spirituality. 1.5 Deliverables: 1.5.1 To provide twenty-four (24) hour residential services to adult offenders that include, but are not limited to: 1. Beds, and meals or meal allowances, or both; 2. Referral services to community support groups and other agencies; 3. Storage and access of offenders to their medication and personal effects; 4. Static and dynamic security; 5. Staff orientation, training and development; 6. Reporting; and 7. Enhanced Services as requested by CSC. 1.5.2 Paper consumption: a. Should printed material be required, double sided printing in black and white format is the default unless otherwise specified by the Project Authority. b. The Contractor must ensure printed material is on paper with a minimum recycled content of 30% and/or certified as originating from a sustainably managed forest. c. The Contractor must recycle unneeded printed documents (in accordance with Security Requirements). 1.6 Constraints: 1.6.1 Location of work: a. The Contractor must perform the work in Brandon, Manitoba. b. Travel i. Travel may be required for the performance of the work under this contract. 1.6.2 Language of Work: The Contractor must perform all work in English, French or both official languages as requested by the offender

ALL OTHER TERMS AND CONDITIONS REMAIN THE SAME _______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 26-58008 Fabrication of Heavy Impact Test Theater Components The National Research Council of Canada’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering Research Centre (NRC-OCRE) has a requirement for the fabrication and delivery of mechanical components for the NRC-OCRE’s Heavy Impact Test Theater (HITT). The requirement includes the manufacturing of a modular Hammer assembly, Anvil assembly, Free Sway System, and Surge Restraint System in accordance with NRC engineering drawings and specifications. BACKGROUND NRC-OCRE is developing the HITT to support full scale ice impact testing. The facility requires precision fabricated structural components including a modular hammer system, a polyethylene anvil assembly, and steel guidance and restraint systems. These components must be manufactured to meet specified design loads while maintaining modularity, durability, and repeatable performance during impact testing. This requirement will provide the fabrication and delivery of the primary structural assemblies required for the HITT facility. REQUIREMENTS The Contractor must fabricate, assemble where applicable, and deliver the following components: 1. Hammer Assembly The Hammer Assembly must consist of a modular welded steel structure designed for impact loading. The assembly includes: • A modular frame composed of sixteen (16) steel cube modules • Stiffened steel plates • Internal load transfer frame components All welds and structural elements must meet the dimensional tolerances and load requirements specified in the NRC drawings. 2. Anvil Assembly The Anvil Assembly consists of a modular polyethylene and aluminum structure designed to interface with the hammer during testing. The assembly includes: • Machined low density polyethylene (LDPE) sheets • Aluminum structural elements • Alignment rods and mounting hardware • Load cell mounting provisions Machining tolerances and surface finishes must comply with the specifications defined in the NRC drawings. 3. Free Sway System The Free Sway System provides guidance and controlled movement of the hammer assembly. The system includes: • Structural steel frame components • Guide rails and carriage assemblies • Mounting interfaces compatible with the hammer system The system must ensure stable alignment and controlled motion during operation. 4. Surge Restraint System The Surge Restraint System is designed to control impact energy and limit structural movement. The system includes: • Structural frame components • Shock absorber integration • Mounting hardware and structural supports The system must be fabricated in accordance with the NRC drawings and designed to withstand repeated dynamic loading. Please refer to tender documents for details. Closing date August 17, 2026 at 2PM EDT

title: Pond Inlet Arctic Char Project Coordination
description: This procurement has been set-aside under the federal government's Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Only Indigenous businesses as defined under PSIB are eligible to challenge the proposed procurement strategy to award the contract to the named Indigenous business. 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Title Pond Inlet Arctic Char 2026 Multi Year Project Coordination 3. Definition of Requirements The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement for the services of Mittimatalik Hunters & Trappers Organization, as a Contractor and a Designated Inuit Organization under the Nunavik Land Claims Agreement, to participate and contribute to the NFR development process. The primary objective of the work is the collection of biological and environmental information for Arctic Char in the Pond Inlet area. The Contractor will be responsible to hire, administer and pay beneficiaries (field workers) on co-operative field research in the Pond Inlet region for the following locations. The Contractor must, but not limited, to the following: 1) ensure all appropriate insurances, including Workers Compensation or an acceptable alternative and accident and liability, have been obtained before work may begin. Proof must be supplied within 14 days of award of the Contract to the Contracting Authority. 2) promptly report any problems to the Project Authority to enable the appropriate action to be taken and ensure that the Contract is completed within the specified Contract period. 3) ensure that beneficiaries understand the requirements and conditions of the Contract and Safety and Harassment policies; and boat operators are aware that they and their boats must meet the safety requirements as set out by Transport Canada. 4) ensure that beneficiaries provide their own bedding and, where necessary, their own tents. 5) retain ownership for all of sampled fish carcasses and is responsible for deciding their disposition and use. 6) Return all field crew, equipment, and samples to Pond Inlet, NU. All information and samples collected from the study shall be transferred to the Project Authority by March 31. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar days posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, DFO/CCG will proceed to a full-tendering process on whether the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the Contract. If no other supplier submits on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a Contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 4. Criteria for Assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (minimum essential requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: For summer: At least ONE (1) of the beneficiaries must: 1) have five (5) years fishing at the designated location (the Pond Inlet area) during the summer and shall act as Boat Captain. 2) have a command of both English and the Inuit language to ensure effective communication between all members of the crew. 3) have a minimum of five (5) years of experience setting and retrieving gill nets. 4) understand the anatomy of fishes sufficiently to dissect fish carcasses to obtain all required measurements. A minimum of five (5) years of fishing experience is required to meet this requirement. 5) have the ability to clearly record, in English, the information collected in the field books provided. 6) have five (5) years of experience working with Arctic Char. For winter: At least TWO (2) of the beneficiaries shall: 1) have a minimum of five (5) years of experience fishing in the Pond Inlet area during the winter, under the ice and shall act as primary field guide. 2) have a command of both English and the Inuit language to ensure effective communication between all members of the crew. 3) have a minimum of five (5) years of experience setting and retrieving gill nets from under the ice 4) understand the anatomy of fishes sufficiently to dissect fish carcasses to obtain all required measurements. A minimum of five (5) years of fishing experience is required to meet this requirement. 5) have the ability to clearly record, in English, the information collected in the field books provided 6) have five (5) years of experience working with Arctic Char. 5. Trade Agreements This procurement is set aside from the international trade agreements under the provision each has for measures with respect to Indigenous peoples or for set-asides for small and minority businesses. 6. Security Requirements This contract does not contain any security requirements. 7. Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier The pre-identified supplier is the only supplier that we are aware of who offers a product which meets all the Minimum Essential Requirements listed above. 8. Exception to the Government Contracts Regulations The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is (are) invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) – “only one person is capable of performing the work.” 9. Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement (CLCA) This requirement is applicable to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement (CLCA). - Nunavut Lands Claim Agreement (1993) 10. Contract Period The Contract period will be from award to April 30, 2028 inclusive and includes an option to extend the contractual period by three (3) periods of one (1) year each. 11. Estimated Cost The estimated value of the Contract is 277,725.00 $ CAD (excluding applicable taxes). 12. Name and Address of the Proposed Contractor Mittamatalik Hunters & Trappers Organization P.O. Box 189 Pond Inlet, Nunavut X0A 0S0 13. Suppliers’ right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the services/goods described herein, may submit a Statement of Capabilities in writing, by e-mail, to the contact person identified in this Notice on or before the closing date and time of this Notice. The Statement of Capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 14. Closing Date The closing date for a submission of a Statement of Capabilities is September 11, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. EDT. 15. Requests for information and submission of statements of capabilities Request for information and statements of capabilities must be sent before the date and time indicated in Article 13, to: Contract Authority mailto: Manon Paulin, Senior Contracting Officer Procurement and Material Management Fisheries and Oceans Canada Telephone : 438-468-3247 Email : DFO.Tenders-Soumissions.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca

title: Contractor for weekly technical support at the Canadian Air and Precipitation Monitoring Program (CAPMoN) Marten River site
description: Description: 1. Summary Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) requires a Contractor for weekly technical support (52 weeks per year) at the Canadian Air and Precipitation Monitoring Program (CAPMoN) Marten River site located approximately 16 kilometers southwest of Marten River, Ontario with coordinates N 46.671194° latitude W 79.919250° longitude. ECCC operates an environmental research and monitoring station in the area which forms part of ECCC’s national network of CAPMoN stations. The primary focus of this monitoring station is the weekly collection of precipitation and/or air samples. Environmental data is collected from both automatic and manual samplers. A contract operator is required to attend to the station to retrieve and process the samples according to the CAPMoN Standard Operating Procedures (SOP's). The samples are then packaged and shipped for analysis to the CAPMoN National Laboratory located in Toronto, Ontario. Other weekly duties include reading and recording of various gauges, diagnostics, and regular servicing, troubleshooting, and minor repair of a variety of monitoring equipment. On-site training will be provided by ECCC technical staff. Details of Work to be Performed: All sampling, shipping, and maintenance must be performed in accordance with the Site Operations Reference Manuals; and in accordance with any amendments to the aforementioned manuals. The routine may involve additional collectors, passive samplers and various climatological and meteorological instruments. ECCC will provide the Contractor the aforementioned manuals and amendments. Initial Contract Period: Date of signed contract to December 31, 2027 – CAPMoN Site Operator that plus two option years. The evaluation and selection methodology is lowest price. 2. Net-Zero Challenge Offerors of Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge. The Net Zero Challenge is a national initiative, led by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), that supports businesses in developing and implementing effective strategies and plans to reduce GHG emissions in facilities and operations to net-zero by 2050. The Net Zero Challenge aligns with Canada's obligations under the Paris Agreement to combat climate change and support Canada's Climate Competitiveness Strategy, which is building a prosperous net-zero future in which Canadian business and industry are well positioned to compete and lead in a global low-carbon economy. Currently, there is a mandatory federal requirement for high-dollar-value procurements. Moving forward, all offerors are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge regardless of the dollar value of the procurement. Offerors who join the Net-Zero Challenge are encouraged to: a. Measure and disclose their greenhouse gas emissions; and b. Commit to planning, setting, and achieving science-based GHG reduction targets aligned with the objectives of the Paris Agreement. Participation in the Net-Zero Challenge not only supports global climate goals but also benefits businesses by positioning them as leaders in a global low-carbon economy. For more information on how to join, please consult the Net-Zero Challenge page. 3. Compliance with Code of Conduct. The Offeror must comply with Canada's Code of Conduct for Procurement 4. Integrity Provisions Offerors must submit certain information for contracts subject to the Ineligibility and Suspension Policy (the policy) at the bid or offer stage. Offerors also have an ongoing obligation to update the Office of Supplier Integrity and Compliance if their information changes. Information to submit with a bid or offer and update as required - Canada.ca 5. Anti-forced Labour Requirements The Offeror states that the Work is not mined, manufactured, or produced wholly or in part by forced labour. In performing the Contract and regardless of who acts as an importer, the Offeror must not, directly or indirectly, deliver Work if it is mined, manufactured, or produced wholly or in part by forced labour. 6. Buy Canadian Policy The Government of Canada has introduced new policies to protect, build, and transform Canadian industries. Check out Buy Canadian Policy for more information on what this could mean for you. 7. Social Procurement Environment and Climate Change Canada supports the Government of Canada’s social and economic objectives, including increasing the participation of businesses from underrepresented groups in government procurement opportunities. As such, offerors owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities, are encouraged to submit a bid for this opportunity. 8. Debriefings Offerors may request a debriefing and feedback on their results of the bid solicitation process. Offerors should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 9. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Offerors may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 10. Additional Information For additional information, interested offerors must contact the Contracting Officer named in this Notice.

title: RFP National Combat Rations Program Long Term Solutions
description: CanadaBuys Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) / Avis de projet de marché (APM) AchatsCanada Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), on behalf of its client, the Department of National Defence (DND), has a requirement under the National Combat Ration Program (NCRP) to procure shelf stable combat rations in accordance with the Statement of Requirement. This requirement is to support Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) training, domestic operations, deployed operations, and emergency situations where the provision of fresh rations is not feasible. Combat rations are consumable, shelf stable products consisting of various food and non food items packaged in an overwrap bag. To fulfil this requirement, Canada has issued one Requests for Proposal (RFP) representing two procurement approaches: •a Prime Vendor approach, under which a single contractor would be responsible for managing all components of the requirement; OR •a Category by Category approach, under which multiple contracts would be awarded by component category, including the designation of a contractor responsible for ration assembly. title: W8472-265978 - DND MARLANT Fuel Barge RFI
description: Canada, as represented by the Department of National Defence (DND), with the assistance of Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), has issued this RFI for the Maritime Forces Atlantic (MARLANT) Fuel Barge requirement (MFB). This RFI is seeking Industry feedback regarding the procurement of a Class approved double-hulled steel tank barge for the fueling of the Canadian Naval Fleet Atlantic (CANFLTANT).Procuring a steel fuel barge for CANFLTLANT will increase operational readiness, allowing for ships to be deployed on short notice. The fuel barge will also decrease fuel wastage during dry dockings as ships can be defueled efficiently. Fuel can then be safely stored and re-purposed for other CANFLTLANT ships. The barge will not be self-propelled. The barge will be transported and positioned by the existing King’s Harbour Master (KHM) tug fleet, including the new Naval Large Tugs (NLT). It would be crewed for day-use (no overnight accommodation) by KHM civilian staff, and the construction and operation would be to commercial Class rules. It is expected that the barge will be berthed at existing jetties.

Chaque accord-cadre est conclu avec un seul opérateur économique et s’exécute par la conclusion de marchés subséquents pour les besoins dont toutes les stipulations contractuelles ne sont pas fixées dans les documents de l’accord-cadre (conformément aux articles R2162-7, R2162-11 et R2162-12 du Code). Les prix indiqués au BPU constituent des prix plafonds pour la conclusion des marchés subséquents. En application de l’article R2162-4 du Code, les prestations d’assistance à maîtrise d’ouvrage faisant l’objet de marchés subséquents sont conclus sans montant minimum d’engagement et avec un montant maximum d’engagement sur sa durée initiale (1 an), à savoir : - Lot 1 : 2 000 000 € HT ; - Lot 2 : 2 000 000 € HT. Ce montant maximum d’engagement s’applique exclusivement aux prestations exécutées au moyen de marchés subséquents et n’inclut pas les prestations de pilotage rémunérées à prix forfaitaire. Il s’agit de marchés publics de prestations intellectuelles qui se réfèrent au Cahier des Clauses Administratives Générales applicable aux marchés publics de prestations intellectuelles (CCAG/PI), approuvé par l’arrêté du 30 mars 2021. title: LMS Cable Gun Lock Procurement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Office of Suicide Prevention, intends to procure Veterans Crisis Line (VCL)-branded cable-style gun locks in support of lethal means safety and secure firearm storage. This effort supports VA suicide prevention by providing secure storage devices that build time and space between impulse and action. The Contractor shall provide 15" heavy-duty steel cable gun locks usable on handguns, rifles, and shotguns, each imprinted with the VCL logo and phone number on both sides. Each unit shall be individually packaged with a VCL wallet card, a VCL crisis-support label affixed to the cable, and use instructions. Locks must be California DOJ-approved, ASTM-compliant, and listed on both the Massachusetts Approved Firearm Safety/Locking Devices list and the Maryland Approved Integrated Mechanical Safety Devices list. Full technical requirements are in the Statement of Work (Section B.2). Estimated total quantity is up to 2,100,000 units (14 truckloads of 150,000 each), consisting of a base requirement of 8 loads (1,200,000 units) and 6 optional loads (900,000 units). Deliveries will be made in installments to the VA Hines Health Care Depot, 5000 South 5th Avenue, Hines, IL 60141-3030. This is a Firm-Fixed-Price acquisition for commercial products conducted under FAR Part 12, using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures. This requirement is 100% set-aside for certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs). Only quotes from firms certified and listed in the SBA certification database at https://certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of quote submission and at award will be considered. NAICS Code: 332510 (Hardware Manufacturing). Size Standard: 750 employees. The period of performance is anticipated to be September 30, 2026, through September 29, 2027. Anticipated award date is on or about September 30, 2026. Questions are due by September 2, 2026, 10:00 AM ET, submitted on Attachment B (Question/Answer Form). Quotes are due by September 11, 2026, 10:00 AM ET. Submit questions and quotes by email to the Contracting Officer, Christopher Binkley, at Christopher.Binkley@va.gov. Interested offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments.

title: R499--RFI School Enrollment Reporting
description: RFI Digital GI Bill and Education Service Automation & Modernization 2 EDUCATION SERVICE DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA) Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) Digital GI Bill (DGIB) and Education Service School Reporting to VBA Date: August 11, 2026 Request for Information Request for Information GI Bill and Education Service School Data Exchange with VBA Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking industry input on solutions to enable secure, standardized data exchange with educational institutions in order to (1) measure the full range of outcomes GI Bill beneficiaries achieve including graduation, persistence, and post-completion employment and earnings and (2) strengthen VBA's ability to proactively identify compliance risks, including violations such as the 85/15 Rule and other indicators of fraud, waste, and abuse. Any proposed solution must minimize reporting burden on schools and training providers and be capable of scaling to accommodate new data requirements as legislative and program needs evolve. This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued for conducting market research and for eliciting industry input as to the Government s requirement to gather/obtain and communicate with educational institutions about students enrolled in the VBA s educational programs. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Proposal/Quote (RFP/RFQ) nor a guarantee that one will ever be issued by the Government; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Do not submit a Quote/Proposal. The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract/order, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the submission of the information being requested, or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. Please do not include a price or proposal in your response. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement (PWS). Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP/RFQ, if issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Background: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), administers education benefits under the GI Bill® program, serving Veterans, servicemembers, and their dependents annually across thousands of educational institutions nationwide. These benefits spanning Chapters 30, 33, 35, and 1606 of Title 38, U.S. Code represent a significant investment in the academic and professional futures of those who have served our country. The current Digital GI Bill (DGIB) ecosystem houses VBA's claims processing systems and supporting data infrastructure. This includes the Data Mart, which houses all education (EDU) benefits data, and CorpDB, which houses all VBA data and enables VBA to produce additional on-demand reports as needed. Despite the scale and importance of these benefits, VBA currently has limited visibility into student outcomes beyond the point of enrollment certification. The data VBA receives from educational institutions today is largely transactional in nature focused on enrollment status, credit hours, and tuition costs and does not provide the longitudinal outcome data necessary to assess whether GI Bill beneficiaries are successfully completing their programs of study, persisting term over term, or achieving the academic and professional outcomes the program is intended to support. Public Law 114-315, Section 404, requires educational institutions that receive payments under the Post-9/11 GI Bill® to report academic progress to VA. Additionally, Executive Order 13607 (2012) requires VA to develop a comprehensive strategy for Servicemember and Veteran student outcome measures that are comparable, to the maximum extent practicable, across federal military and Veterans educational benefit programs. VA has previously explored outcome measure types such as retention rate, persistence rate, transfer-out rate, graduation rate, and certificate of completion, and welcomes industry input on additional or alternative approaches to satisfying these requirements. This data gap has meaningful consequences across two critical areas: Outcome Measurement VBA is committed to understanding whether GI Bill education benefits are producing positive, measurable outcomes for Veterans and their dependents not only during enrollment, but beyond it. Without reliable, standardized data from educational institutions and other authoritative sources on indicators such as graduation rates, academic persistence, program completion, and post-completion outcomes including employment and earnings, VBA cannot fully assess program effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, or demonstrate the full impact of GI Bill investments on Veterans' academic and professional success. Compliance Oversight VBA has a statutory responsibility to ensure that GI Bill benefits are administered in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, and that educational institutions participating in the program meet required standards including compliance with the 85/15 Rule and other statutory and regulatory requirements. Enhanced data exchange with educational institutions would allow VBA to proactively identify discrepancies between school-reported data and VA records, detect potential fraud, waste, and abuse earlier, and support audit and oversight functions. Beyond protecting Veterans and their dependents from bad actors within the program, this enhanced visibility would also allow VBA to recognize and champion educational institutions that consistently demonstrate strong outcomes and program compliance. To address these gaps, VBA is exploring industry recommendations and guidance on solutions that would enable secure, standardized, and scalable data exchange between educational institutions, other public and private entities and VBA. The envisioned solution would allow schools to provide VBA with structured outcome and enrollment data on GI Bill beneficiaries on a regular basis, reducing manual reporting burden on School Certifying Officials (SCOs) while significantly enhancing VBA's ability to measure program outcomes and fulfill its compliance mission. EVALUATION AND AWARD In accordance with RFO 12.203, the Government will evaluate quotations on an individual line-item basis. Award may be made to more than one quoter, and more than one line item may be awarded to the same quoter. The Government will make award to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforms to the solicitation and provides the best value to the Government, considering the following evaluation factors: Technical conformity; Past performance; and Price. Technical conformity and past performance are equal in importance. When combined, technical conformity and past performance are significantly more important than price. Technical conformity will be evaluated based on the quoted product�s compliance with the applicable item description, quantity, packaging requirements, delivery requirements, Certified Menu Specifications, BOP Religious Diet Specifications, and all other solicitation requirements. A quotation that fails to meet a mandatory requirement will not be considered for award for the affected line item. Past performance will be evaluated based on its relevance and quality. The Government may consider past-performance information from any available source, including information provided by the quoter, CPARS, Government records, references, and commercial sources. A quoter without relevant past performance will receive a neutral past-performance assessment. The Government will conduct a best-value tradeoff and may select a higher-priced quotation when the benefits associated with superior technical conformity or past performance justify the additional price. As differences among quotations under the non-price factors become less significant, price will become increasingly important. The Government is not required to select the lowest-priced quotation and will not pay a price premium when the superiority of a higher-priced quotation does not provide a meaningful benefit to the Government. Prices must include all transportation and delivery charges to the FOB destination. Unit prices may be quoted to no more than four decimal places. Extended prices must be stated in dollars and cents. All boxes and cases must be properly labeled. Handwritten, crossed-out, altered, or illegible product labels will not be accepted. Deliveries must be palletized unless different arrangements have been approved in advance by FCI Bastrop warehouse personnel. Refrigerated, nonfrozen perishable foods must be delivered at a temperature between 34�F and 40�F. Canned goods must be delivered above 34�F and must not be frozen. Frozen food products must arrive fully frozen and before any applicable best-by, sell-by, use-by, or freeze-by date shown on the label. Products showing evidence of prior thawing, temperature abuse, damaged packaging, or contamination will be refused. All products will be inspected for compliance with the solicitation and resulting purchase order. The Government may thaw, cook, or otherwise examine product samples when necessary to determine compliance with the applicable specifications. Receipt may be conditional for up to three business days to permit adequate examination and testing. Products that fail to comply with the applicable specifications or other award requirements may be refused or rejected. Deliveries will be accepted Mondays only from 7:30 a.m. through 10:00 am Central Time, Monday through Friday, excluding weekends and Federal holidays. Holidays that fall on Mondays will be the next day. Deliveries will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis unless FCI Bastrop provides different delivery instructions. A delivery appointment is not required unless otherwise directed by FCI Bastrop warehouse personnel. description: Combined Synopsis-Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services Effective Date: 01/15/2026 Revision: 03 Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01. This solicitation is set aside for FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334510, with a small business size standard of 1,250 Employees The FSC/PSC is 6515. The Providence VA Medical Center 850 Chalkstone Avenue Providence, RI 02908-4734 is seeking to purchase the following items from below. The Providence Medical Center is seeking (1) AMPA ONE System portable transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) or Equal. This is a new brand name or equal requirement. US Made TMS Preference as long at it meets the salient characteristics. All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: Supplies/Services Description Quantity Unit of Measure Ampa One portable transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) 1 EA Purchase of Neuronavigation Caps (small) Pack of 10 1 EA Purchase of Neuronavigation Caps (medium) Pack of 10 1 EA Purchase of Neuronavigation Caps (large) Pack of 10 1 EA Purchase of Neuronavigation Caps (x-large) Pack of 10 1 EA DELIVERY LOCATION: Providence VA Medical Center 850 Chalkstone Avenue Providence, RI 02908-4734 FOB: Destination Statement of Work Brand Name Ampa One TMS or Equal (with U.S. Made Preference) Description of Requirement The Providence VA Medical Center requires a portable, lightweight, inpatient suitable Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) system, procured as Brand Name Ampa One TMS or Equal. Inpatient psychiatric units impose strict physical, safety, and workflow limitations that necessitate a compact, mobile, rapidly deployable neurostimulation system. Systems designed for outpatient clinics workstation style consoles, tethered cooling systems, or large immobile units are not compatible with inpatient psychiatric constraints A U.S. Made Preference applies to this acquisition under applicable Buy American requirements. Domestic products meeting all salient characteristics will be given preference; however, foreign-made systems may still be considered if they meet all mandatory characteristics and no acceptable U.S. made alternative is identified. 2. Inpatient Clinical Use Requirements The offered TMS system Ampa One or Equal must fully support the following inpatient workflows: Rapid bedside neurostimulation for patients who cannot safely transfer due to psychiatric acuity, mobility restrictions, elopement risk, or observation requirements. High acuity, time limited schedules, requiring rapid movement of the system between multiple rooms throughout the day. Flexible deployment in multi use areas such as therapy rooms, provider consult spaces, and medical evaluation rooms. Consistent and reproducible coil placement without reliance on bulky or measurement intensive positioning equipment 3. Inpatient Environmental & Safety Constraints The system must be suitable for psychiatric inpatient environments with space and safety constraints: Small patient rooms with limited clearance around beds, medical equipment, and anti ligature furniture. Narrow hallways unsuitable for workstation style systems. Shared rooms where permanently installed systems are not permitted. Ceiling height limitations, restricted outlet placement, ligature risk mitigation requirements, constant observation protocols, and fall risk considerations none compatible with large or fixed TMS consoles. 4. Required Device Characteristics (Salient Characteristics Mandatory Minimums) To be considered equal, offered systems must meet or exceed all salient characteristics of the Ampa One TMS. A. Mobility & Physical Design Generator weight must not exceed 45 pounds. Generator must include integrated wheels for rapid room to room maneuverability. System must deploy without any permanent construction, workstation chairs, anchoring, or bulky cooling devices. System must fit through narrow inpatient corridors and small psychiatric patient rooms. Must include neuronavigation caps (small, medium, large, x large). Must include TMS system maintenance for a minimum of 3 years. B. Coil Requirements L coil must not exceed 10 pounds. Coil positioning must be camera guided or equivalent, eliminating manual measurement procedures. Must support FDA cleared geometries, including iTBS (3 minute) and 20 minute bilateral/dorsomedial prefrontal protocols. C. Clinical Safety & Efficiency Passive thermal management no external cooling infrastructure permitted. Simple tablet based interface to enable rapid staff training and avoid workflow disruption. Must comply with inpatient psychiatric safety requirements, including anti ligature, constant visibility, and secure use protocols. D. Patient Safety Must support in place treatment to reduce elopement risk, agitation, and fall risk by eliminating the need to transport patients to other clinic areas. E. Impact of Non Compliant Systems Large outpatient workstation style systems: Cannot be maneuvered in constrained inpatient spaces. Would prevent inpatient TMS services, delaying care and worsening outcomes. Would impose unacceptable IT and security burdens due to networked consoles and cooling systems. Would fail to meet inpatient deployment and safety requirements 5. U.S. Made Preference (Buy American Compliance) Domestic end products meeting all salient characteristics will be evaluated favorably. Vendors must identify the place of manufacture for the TMS system and all neuronavigation caps. Foreign made systems may only be considered if no domestic product meets the salient characteristics at fair and reasonable pricing. 6. Deliverables Complete TMS system meeting all salient characteristics Neuronavigation caps (S/M/L/XL) Operator manuals and quick start guides Warranty & maintenance documentation (minimum 3 years) Training (on site or virtual) for clinical staff 7.
